article.name: AgentOS
article.summary: AgentOS is a TypeScript agent framework whose cognitive-memory layer encodes scoped traces, retrieves and assembles context, and can connect memory to working, graph, archive, and SQL-backed stores. This is a source review, not an execution or performance assessment.

who_what.text: The official repository describes AgentOS as a TypeScript AI agent framework; its README identifies `@framers/agentos` as the core runtime and includes cognitive memory. The repository is under the framerslab GitHub organization; this review makes no claim about an individual maintainer.

architecture.text: `CognitiveMemoryManager` coordinates trace encoding, retrieval, prompt assembly, working memory, optional graph and typed-network components, health reporting, and deletion. The GMI runtime builds cognitive memory from agent options and connects it to each session; `agentCognitiveMemory.ts` wires embeddings, an in-memory vector store, a knowledge graph, and optionally a persistent Brain/archive.

A `MemoryTrace` stores content, type, scope and scope ID, timestamps, tags/entities, encoding and access fields, emotional context, provenance, and a source-derived trust policy. Provenance records source type/time, confidence, verification count and optional source/contradiction references. The policy separately gates authorization, personalization and factual-claim use.

The documented storage layer uses the `@framers/sql-storage-adapter` abstraction and supports SQLite, Postgres and other runtime adapters; memory overview describes traces, indexes, graph data, retrieval feedback, consolidation records and optional verbatim archives. These are architecture statements from documentation, not measurements of capacity or portability.

behavior.text: Write: `encode()` creates an episodic trace by default (or uses caller-provided type/scope), defaults provenance to `user_statement`, applies the source-type trust policy, stores the trace and focuses it in working memory. Optional mechanisms, graph registration and typed-network extraction are separate configured paths; typed-network extraction is off by default.

Update/correction: traces have `updatedAt` and provenance fields, but this inspection did not establish a general in-place correction history contract for `encode()`. AgentOS also exposes correction and memory lifecycle APIs elsewhere; their guarantees depend on which facade and configuration the host uses. Do not infer current-value accuracy from the presence of these fields.

Delete: manager deletion removes named traces or a scope and invokes cleanup for graph, archive and typed facts. The persistent facade removes graph copies before rows and updates indexes; higher-level subject erasure writes a tombstone, attempts the mind/store/pages/sessions, and reports which parts were reached or missed. The report explicitly leaves the host's own conversation history, out-of-scope ingested documents and organization-scope memory outside that subject deletion path.

Retrieval: dense retrieval is the default. Optional hybrid mode runs dense, exact-word and recency legs, fuses ranks, deduplicates and cuts to top K; a configured reranker may reorder candidates. Prompt assembly applies a token budget. Capture mode can retain per-leg ranks, timings and reranker data; these source-visible fields do not establish measured quality or latency.

metrics.evidence: Source inspection describes retrieval and confidence-policy hooks but no eligible adjudicated answerable or unsupported probe results for this review.
No current-value adjudication or post-correction probes were run; trace metadata and correction APIs alone do not establish stale-value rates.
Deletion code has explicit cleanup paths and reached/missed reporting, but no post-delete probes or runtime erasure were run here.

Conversation scope keys encode agent plus user, anonymous-session, or operator identity, and GMI documents session/user scoping. This source review did not exercise authorization boundaries or cross-scope leak probes.
Trace provenance and trust policy can constrain whether traces support factual claims. No answer captures were adjudicated for support precision or resolvable citation coverage.

metrics.domain: Latency, write-to-recall delay, tokens, cost, and storage
metrics.evidence: Code exposes optional recall leg timings and capture data, but this review ran no workload and measured none of these resource or delay domains.

limits.text: This review inspected selected documentation and source files at one verified repository revision. It does not establish runtime correctness, adapter-specific behavior, security isolation, deletion completeness, quality, operational reliability or performance.

AgentOS has multiple memory facades and configuration paths. A host's actual behavior depends on selected runtime, stores, enabled mechanisms, retrieval policy, providers and deletion wiring; this bounded review does not audit every path.
The roster supplied ordinal identity, repository locator and Atlas attribution only. Atlas descriptions, feature marks and layout were not used as assessment evidence.
